clips.title: The story
paras: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills is a Horde courier task connecting the Forsaken research efforts in Silverpine Forest with their outpost in Tarren Mill. Entrusted with sensitive notes from Apothecary Renferrel, the traveler journeys south into the disputed Hillsbrad Foothills to deliver vital biological research to Apothecary Lydon. This dispatch reflects the intense pressure Lady Sylvanas Windrunner places upon the Royal Apothecary Society to produce a weapon of mass devastation.

Since breaking free from the Lich King's iron grip, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has harbored a single-minded ambition: the development of a New Plague engineered to eradicate both living enemies and the Scourge. To achieve this, the Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from the Banshee Queen. Because distance isolates their laboratories, researchers scattered across Lordaeron must continuously share raw chemical data and test findings to accelerate their sinister breakthrough.

Apothecary Renferrel, operating out of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, directs couriers to deliver his recent findings to his colleague, Apothecary Lydon. The trek winds south through the shadowed pine woods and down into the open, rolling pastures of Hillsbrad Foothills. There, nestled beneath the Alterac Mountains, lies Tarren Mill—a vital Forsaken hub and laboratory staging ground.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: The Royal Apothecary Society is under extreme pressure from the Dark Lady to develop a New Plague. We are working diligently and have made much progress. It is our belief that the success will be achieved much faster if we share information amongst the Society.
For that reason I want you to deliver my latest findings to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, a small town nestled in the Hillsbrad Foothills. The journey will be a long one.
Head south and stick to the roads. Follow the signs closely!

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah, most excellent. Apothecary Renferrel has my utmost respect. I am anxious to study his work.
